seoTitle: Saint Paul Public Schools Calendar: SPPS Dates & PDFs
seoDescription: Reviewed SPPS dates, staggered Pre-K/K opening, quarter endings, MEA and seasonal breaks, grade-specific conference days, and five language PDFs.
districtFact: Saint Paul Public Schools serves approximately 33,000 students across 68 schools. The 2026–27 family calendar uses separate grades 1–12 and Pre-K/K openings, four quarters, PreK–5-only conference dates, and official PDFs in English, Hmong, Karen, Somali, and Spanish.

about.title: A Citywide District with More Than 114 Languages
about.content: SPPS reports approximately 33,000 students across 68 schools, with students speaking more than 114 languages. Its official family calendar is published in five languages.

about.title: The School Year Opens in Two Stages
about.content: Grades 1-12 begin on the Tuesday after Labor Day. Pre-K and kindergarten use that Tuesday and Wednesday for Welcome Meetings, then start classes Thursday. Early Childhood Special Education follows the Pre-K calendar, so ECSE families should not use the grades 1-12 opening date.

about.title: Some No-School Days Stop at Grade 5
about.content: The green dates in the SPPS PDF apply only to PreK-5. Grades 6-12 remain in session, including grades 6-8 housed inside PreK-8 schools. Other conference and staff dates are blue and apply to all grades, so the color and grade column matter as much as the event name.

about.title: Four Quarters, but Different Work at Each Level
about.content: SPPS prints four quarter endings. The student-free date after a quarter may serve different purposes by level: elementary professional development or conferences, and secondary grading or professional development. Families share the closure even when staff assignments differ.

about.title: Saint Paul's Public-School Story Began Before Statehood
about.content: The district traces its roots to Saint Paul's first public school, opened by Harriet Bishop in 1847, and to the first elected school board in 1856. The current calendar therefore belongs to a long-running city school system, not a countywide or suburban district.

calendarNotes: The SPPS family calendar should be read by grade band. Grades 1-12 begin first; Pre-K, kindergarten, and ECSE follow the Welcome Meeting sequence and begin two days later. Blue dates close school for all grades, while green conference dates close only PreK-5. On those green dates, grades 6-8 at PreK-8 schools remain in session along with other secondary students. The calendar uses four quarters and often places a student-free conference, development, or grading day next to a quarter ending. Each published future year has official English, Hmong, Karen, Somali, and Spanish PDFs. Individual school events, bell times, activities, and program-specific instructions still require the school calendar or direct communication.

planningTips.title: Planning with the SPPS Calendar
content: Use the student's grade or program for September: grades 1-12 start Tuesday, while Pre-K, kindergarten, and ECSE start Thursday after two Welcome Meeting days.
Treat green PreK-5 conference dates as partial-district closures. Grades 6-12 are in session, even when grades 6-8 attend a building labeled PreK-8.
Treat blue conference, development, grading, holiday, and break dates as no school for all students from Pre-K through grade 12.
Do not assume every quarter-ending date is a student closure. Quarter 1 and Quarter 3 can end on regular school days, while the nearby staff or conference date carries the no-school status.
Winter Break crosses New Year's Day; read the complete date range rather than counting only the December portion printed in the month list.
Choose English, Hmong, Karen, Somali, or Spanish from the official calendar hub. These are translations of the same attendance calendar, not separate school tracks.
Use the live SPPS calendar filter or the student's school site for activities, Board events, school-specific conferences, and schedule changes beyond the one-page family calendar.

livingHere.intro: SPPS serves Minnesota's capital as a single-city district whose calendar and language access reflect Saint Paul's neighborhoods, immigrant communities, and range of school designs.

highlights.label: 68 schools
highlights.detail: The district reports a citywide network spanning elementary, middle, high, non-traditional, care-and-treatment, and special-education settings.

highlights.label: About 33,000 students
highlights.detail: SPPS identifies itself as Minnesota's second-largest school district.

highlights.label: More than 114 student languages
highlights.detail: The district's language diversity is reflected in multilingual learning, immersion programs, family councils, and translated calendars.

highlights.label: PreK-8 campuses
highlights.detail: Some buildings span elementary and middle grades, which is why the calendar explicitly says grades 6-8 still attend on PreK-5-only closure dates.

highlights.label: District 625
highlights.detail: Official contact information identifies the system as Saint Paul Public Schools, District 625, headquartered on Colborne Street.

highlights.label: Since 1856
highlights.detail: Saint Paul's first school board was established before Minnesota became a state.

districtFaqs.q: Do all SPPS students start school on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: No. Grades 1-12 begin Tuesday after Labor Day. Pre-K and kindergarten have Welcome Meetings Tuesday and Wednesday, then begin Thursday. ECSE follows the Pre-K calendar.

districtFaqs.q: What does a green no-school date mean on the SPPS calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Green means no school for PreK-5 only. Grades 6-12 remain in session, including grades 6-8 at schools that serve PreK-8.

districtFaqs.q: Does SPPS use semesters or quarters?
districtFaqs.a: The reviewed family calendars use four quarters. The PDFs print quarter endings in November, January, spring, and on the last day of school.

districtFaqs.q: What is MEA on the SPPS calendar?
districtFaqs.a: SPPS labels two October no-school days for the statewide teacher meeting, commonly called MEA. The closure applies to PreK-12.

districtFaqs.q: Which languages are the SPPS calendar PDFs available in?
districtFaqs.a: For 2026-27 and 2027-28, SPPS publishes official calendars in English, Hmong, Karen, Somali, and Spanish.

districtFaqs.q: Are all school events included in the printable SPPS calendar?
districtFaqs.a: No. The one-page PDF focuses on districtwide and grade-band attendance dates. Use the official live calendar and the student's school site for campus events, bell times, activities, and detailed conference schedules.

customSections.label: The SPPS Color Key Is an Attendance Rule
customSections.content: The PDF uses its color legend to separate three different attendance situations. Reading only the words No School can lead to an incorrect childcare or transportation plan.

customSections.label: Five Official Family Calendar Languages
customSections.content: SPPS publishes both future-year family calendars in English, Hmong, Karen, Somali, and Spanish. The translated PDFs preserve the same color key and grade-band structure, which is especially important for PreK-5-only dates.

customSections.label: What the One-Page Calendar Does Not Cover
customSections.content: The family PDF is the attendance-date baseline. SPPS also operates online, non-traditional, care-and-treatment, transition, special-education, early-childhood, and community-education programs. Families in those settings should verify program instructions rather than assuming every operational detail follows the general PDF.
